svg.aria-label: The intercept room: anatomy of the leaderboard claims
svg.text: The intercept room: anatomy of the leaderboard claims
Damascus, 1965: a hidden transmitter is found by silencing every other signal and listening for the one still on air.
We did the same with every leader's method note: silence all but one ingredient, measure on folds it never saw, and listen.
Sources: verbatim leaderboard notes (13 Oct) · experiments 102-108 · 265 cross-validation runs · numbers read from the evidence files
1 · The transmissions: what each leader claims
Each mast is one method note. Each chip is one ingredient it names, coloured by what our tests found.
✗ tested on our data: no gain
worse than our production on 5 of 5 seeds
worse than our production on 5 of 5 seeds
worse than our production on 5 of 5 seeds
worse than our production on 5 of 5 seeds
2 · The blackout method: how a claim is tested
Same five steps for every claim, so results are comparable and can be re-run by anyone with the repository.
unknowns fixed in a frozen protocol
one ingredient changes at a time
rule v2 must pass on all five
Why the blackout matters: on 81 test flows a single facebook flow moves a score by about 2 points, so only paired runs on identical folds can hear a real signal under the noise.
3 · Signal strength: what each method is worth on our data
Change in macro F1 against our production on the same folds (mean of 5 never-used seeds). Left of the line = weaker than what we already have.
T1 not part of the claim
T2 not part of the claim
T2 not part of the claim
T1 not part of the claim
4 · Hidden transmitters: what the leaders might not say
Notes are written for rivals to read. These are the signals that could really be behind a 95, and what our tests say.
5 uploads a day on the ranking set
Their v8→v9 jump is exactly +2 flows;
a blind swap gives that in 1-2% of tries (105)
the Cohen move: use the context
A Task 1 of 0.94 is our model's
5 · Where the story fits, and what we have
The analogy explains the hard part of the data; the evidence explains the decision.
facebook and instagram share Meta's network stack, so their first-5
openings are often identical; google and youtube share QUIC.
Does not fit: context finds the spy
In the story the context gave him away. Here the context is capture time:
excluded by our rules, and it makes predictions worse anyway (107).
Does not fit: most Task 1 errors
They are not identical signals but too few examples (facebook 11,
instagram 19 labelled flows); most remaining errors are confident (093).
Production stays: Task 1 CV 0.85, Task 2 CV 0.76, board 87.24 (rank 8).
Gap to first: 7.77 points ≈ 5 Task 1 flows + 2 Task 2 flows of 81.
Every ingredient is ours already, no gain, or off-limits.
Decision: no upload; finish the technical report.
